method: Two phones only: persistence, deferred delivery, receipts, tombstones and duplicate suppression. This is NOT multi-hop validation. Raw: dtn_log.txt, phone_*_val.jsonl, bench_phone_*/bench/events_*.jsonl.

steps: PHONE_B Emergency mode stopped; PHONE_A has no session
PHONE_A queues 5 trusted messages (tag DTN1, 120 B) to PHONE_B -> 5 LOCAL bundles, 4 copy tokens each, state QUEUED
PHONE_A app force-stopped and restarted -> all 5 still QUEUED in the durable store
store_carry_forward.result: 5/5 delivered to PHONE_B, each exactly once; all 5 DELIVERED on PHONE_A (verified signed receipts)

cleanup: After a few inventory rounds both stores held zero bundles: PHONE_A's originals and PHONE_B's receipt copies were removed by tombstones.

duplicate_suppression.whole_session: PHONE_B inbox 160 = sum of all A->B runs; PHONE_A inbox 105 = sum of all B->A runs; 0 duplicate delivery events across 265 messages

survived_app_restart_and_reinstall: 34 messages stalled by the lifetime-cap bug stayed QUEUED across reinstall + restart and delivered after the fix (run A2B)
rate_limit_finding: Destination copies (messages AND receipts) are limited to 16 per session per sliding minute (ProtocolConfig.maxDestinationClaimsPerSession). With both directions active, receipts double the demand, so above ~8 messages/min/direction deliveries queue behind the limit (run A2Bq/B2Aq p95 queued->RELAYED 58 s). This is a tunable abuse limit, not a fault.
